articles.title: Heat is on Carrick but Wilcox must share blame for Manchester United’s woes
articles.summary: Recruitment is under scrutiny after £155m was spent on three midfielders while other positions were neglected. There was a mix of boos and apathy as Manchester United slumped out of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday in their latest depressing act in domestic cup competitions.
body: This is the natural course of football, where supporters know what is good or bad and give a rapid opinion to those whose wages they deem they pay. Carrick and his charges are the face of the club, the ones put up to speak with journalists and sent to promote the wares of sponsors.
The head coach is often viewed as accountable for everything, from tactics to transfers, but the picture is more complex.

Carrick returned to United in January, but others have overseen the long-term strategy, within which the head coach sits. Pressure comes with his job, though, and a loss at Fulham on Sunday would significantly increase it.

United’s fanbase is fully aware of those running the club, with regular protests against the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. They realise not everything happening over 90 minutes is the fault of the head coach and those wearing the shirt. The boos are for the one-off performance, the apathy for the bigger picture. It is tough for United supporters to see their club, back in the Champions League, outspent in the summer by promoted sides but this is the reality after years of financial mismanagement. It means the funds available have to be spent wisely.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola makes Bournemouth return still learning on the job at Liverpool
articles.summary: Making big decisions and turning draws into wins is vital as head coach looks to improve on a mixed start with Reds. Alisson made little attempt to sugarcoat Liverpool’s unbeaten start to the season under Andoni Iraola when analysing the draw against Fulham with the club’s in-house media.
body: Big things are the target and big things are expected from a Liverpool side containing three £100m-plus forwards. But the learning curve under the new head coach is proving challenging. As it is for the new head coach, too. Big decisions appear unavoidable.

When Iraola faces his former club Bournemouth on Sunday for the first time since ending his impressive three-year reign there last season, he is likely to know more about the opposition players than his own. “It’s going to be a tricky one because they know very well what we try to do,” Iraola admitted. “But I also know their strengths and weaknesses. It’s going to be strange for me.”

Iraola spent more than two hours debriefing Marco Rose, his successor at the Vitality Stadium, on the Bournemouth squad and staff in June. They had time for a smooth handover because, as Iraola put it, his exit from the club “was so clean” and he decided to stay on the south coast while his two young children finished school. Whether they discussed how Bournemouth became the draw specialists of last season remains private.

articles.title: The man who would be king - the rise and fall of 'the next Prince Naseem'
articles.summary: Touted as the king to Naseem Hamed's prince, Daniel Teasdale's story is instead a cautionary tale.
body: Boxer Daniel Teasdale was hailed as the heir to the legendary Prince Naseem Hamed, but his promise never materialised into fame, fortune and films.
"He's better than Naz at the same age," said trainer Brendan Ingle.
Hamed had won his first world title aged 21. Teasdale was still a teenager.
Ingle, from his gym in Sheffield, moulded the careers of a conveyor belt of world-beaters and title winners. He guided both of the fighters from childhood.

articles.title: Brentford batter Chelsea 3-0 as Colwill admits Blues were “bullied” and must improve
articles.summary: Levi Colwill has admitted that Chelsea were 'bullied' by Brentford during the club's 3-0 defeat to their West London neighbours. Chelsea crashed to defeat at Brentford on Friday night as the Bees ran riot at the Gtech Community Stadium.
body: Xabi Alonso's side were exposed defensively again in another reality check for the new head coach. Brentford scored three times in a punishing second half, with Jaidon Anthony opening the scoring with a close-range header on 61 minutes, as Chelsea failed to deal with a deep corner kick.

The hosts had a second when Igor Thiago turned in on the rebound, after Kevin Schade 's initial effort had been saved by Emi Martinez. Brentford cut apart Chelsea to send Schade in on goal, after the Blues squandered possession.
Substitute Fabio Carvalho wrapped up the win when he added a third in stoppage time to seal a big Brentford win.

Reflecting on the result, stand-in Chelsea captain Colwill said his side had been 'bullied' at set pieces. The result continues a concerning defensive record for Chelsea, who have conceded a Premier League high of 12 goals ahead of this weekend's fixtures.

articles.title: From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary
articles.summary: From obscurity and near oblivion to Premier League and Europe - Brighton celebrate their 125th anniversary.
body: It is Thursday, 9 November, 2023. Brighton manager Roberto de Zerbi is addressing his players in the Amsterdam Arena before their Europa League tie with Ajax.
"There's 3,000 Brighton fans in this stadium tonight," said the Italian. "But there's more than twice that number in the city who have travelled over. Remember that when you go on to that pitch."
A long-standing senior Brighton official was in the dressing room that day. A fan first and foremost, but someone who has spent almost three decades working for the club.
"It made the hairs on the back of my neck stand up," he said.

articles.title: 'Bullied' and 'out of control' - Chelsea's defensive issues laid bare
articles.summary: "You need to feel it. We're not feeling it," said Xabi Alonso after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford. Yet Chelsea are stuck in a familiar feeling.
body: Another defeat, their 11th of the calendar year - more than they had in 2025, with three months of this year to go. At least two goals conceded for the fifth straight Premier League game under Alonso. More set-piece woe.

"We dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," said Alonso. That will concern Chelsea fans the most. It was way too easy for Brentford to take over that second half.
And there's another continuing trend: Chelsea being outbattled in a match. Remember, they were outrun in the vast majority of their Premier League matches last season.

The first thing you think about when you come up against Brentford is set pieces. Long throws, smart corners - the lot. And just like against Hull in their previous game, Chelsea lost control of the match by conceding once again from a set-piece.

articles.title: How belief of Wakefield's inner sanctum led to history-making semi-final
articles.summary: When Wakefield Trinity came back into Super League for the 2025 season, there wouldn't have been many who would have foreseen a semi-final appearance within two seasons- except those in their inner sanctum.
body: That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

An example of turning that raw talent into a shining diamond? Caleb Hamlin-Uele. Wakefield saw something in a player who was not breaking through in the NRL. They brought him into the Championship, moulded him, made him one of Super League's best props, and now he is truly in contention to represent England at the World Cup this autumn.
Of course, the biggest success of all would be a trophy. But for now, they are through to their first ever Super League semi-final after their 26-16 victory over Leigh in the Eliminators.
